name: Nikon Mount Adapter FTZ II
summary: F-mount to Z-mount adapter with no optics and no AF motor. AF works only with lenses that have their own motor (AF-S, AF-P, AF-I). Screw-drive AF and AF-D lenses become manual focus with an electronic rangefinder. Same function as the FTZ, without the tripod foot.

effects.af_impact: No AF motor in the adapter. AF-S, AF-P and AF-I lenses autofocus. Nikon warns AF may be slower and may fail on dark or low-contrast subjects in some combinations, and lists three DX lenses (18-55 VR, 18-55 VR II, 55-200 IF-ED) that may need repeated AF attempts.
effects.notes: Purely mechanical and electrical adapter with no glass, so no optical effect.

compatibility_classes.vr: Lens VR works if present. Body IBIS combines with it (see stabilization).

compatibility_classes.notes: Focus position may shift if the camera is turned off and on after focusing.

compatibility_classes.aperture: Camera-controlled (lock the aperture ring at minimum)
compatibility_classes.vr: None in lens. Body IBIS on Z8 and Z5II.

compatibility_classes.af: Yes if AF-S or AF-P. No if screw-drive AF G.

compatibility_classes.aperture: Camera-controlled. Set the aperture ring to minimum aperture before mounting.
compatibility_classes.vr: No lens VR. Body IBIS 3-axis on Z8 and Z5II.

compatibility_classes.vr: Body IBIS on Z8 and Z5II

compatibility_classes.exposure_modes: A and M (per Nikon table; reading of a garbled table)

compatibility_classes.metering: Yes. Highlight-weighted falls back to center-weighted.
compatibility_classes.vr: Body IBIS on Z8 and Z5II. Enter focal length and max aperture in Non-CPU lens data so IBIS and EXIF are correct.

stabilization.non_vr_f_lenses: Z8 and Z5II: 3-axis in-body correction (yaw, pitch, roll), per Nikon's FTZ II product page as recorded in the existing lens record f-af-micro-60-f28d. Not re-fetched here. Z50II: none (no IBIS).
stabilization.vr_f_lenses: Lens VR handles pitch and yaw. Nikon's FTZ guide says in-camera VR works together with lens VR across pitch, yaw and roll, and the lens VR switch takes precedence.
stabilization.synchro_vr: Not supported with F lenses (Nikon FTZ guide).
stabilization.focus_point_vr: Z5II Focus-point VR needs non-VR NIKKOR Z lenses, so it is not available with F lenses.

limitations: Z TELECONVERTER TC-1.4x and TC-2.0x cannot be used with the FTZ or FTZ II.
F-mount AF-S and AF-I teleconverters work only with Nikon's listed lenses. AF may be slower or fail in low contrast.
Focus shift shooting works with AF-S and AF-P lenses only. Focus position auto reset is disabled and no peaking stack image is recorded.
Save/Recall focus position roles are disabled with F lenses.
The Auto Capture 'Distance' criterion (Z8) may not work well with F lenses.
Vignette control and Auto distortion control have no effect on PC-E, AI-P, PC Micro, non-CPU and older non-G/E/D AF lenses.
The electronic rangefinder may be inaccurate with some AF-S, AF-P and AF-I lenses. AF fine-tune may help.
Non-CPU lenses: enter Non-CPU lens data (focal length, max aperture) for correct IBIS and EXIF.
Third-party F-mount lenses (Sigma, Tokina, Zeiss ZF.2, Voigtländer SL II) are not covered by Nikon's guide. Behavior is unverified.
mf_subject_detection_with_f_lenses: Z8 (FW 3.00+), Z5II and Z50II have MF subject detection. Nikon sources fetched here do not say whether F lenses on the FTZ II are supported. J.M. Peltier (Zf/Z6III) reports that it works with non-CPU and CPU F lenses, that the ERF works with CPU lenses that pass distance data, and that some AF-D lenses are uncertain. Low confidence for the owner's bodies.

compatible_lenses.on_ftz_ii: MF only with electronic rangefinder. Metering and all exposure modes work. Body IBIS 3-axis on Z8 and Z5II. Focus shift shooting not supported (not AF-S/AF-P).
Full AF. All modes. Body IBIS 3-axis on Z8 and Z5II. Focus shift shooting supported.
MF only with electronic rangefinder. Body IBIS 3-axis on Z8 and Z5II. Set the aperture ring to minimum.
MF only with electronic rangefinder. Body IBIS 3-axis on Z8 and Z5II.
Has its own motor, so AF is expected, but it is not in Nikon's guide. Behavior unverified here.

compatible_lenses.on_ftz_ii: Manual focus. Nikon's table for comparable AI-P lenses lists modes A and M only. Unverified for ZF.2.

If it is the F-mount screw-drive AT-X Pro D, MF only. Unverified.

field_tips: Screw-drive lenses (AF-D Micro 60, DC 105, 50 f/1.8D) are manual focus on every Z body. Use the green focus-point indicator or magnified view and focus peaking.
Lock the aperture ring at minimum (largest f-number) on D lenses before mounting, or the camera will show an error.
On the Z50II there is no IBIS, so non-VR F lenses are unstabilized. Raise the shutter speed.
For focus stacking with F glass, only AF-S and AF-P lenses (e.g. the 85 f/1.4G) work with in-camera focus shift.
The Z teleconverter will not fit through the FTZ II.

sources.name: Nikon: Using F-mount NIKKOR lenses with the FTZ II/FTZ mount adapter (PDF, SB3J11(11))
sources.findings: Compatibility table by lens class. AF-P focus-shift-after-power-cycle note. Focus shift works with AF-S/AF-P but auto reset is disabled. Z TCs cannot be used. No Synchro VR. Save/Recall focus position disabled. The Auto Capture Distance criterion may not work. Vignette and distortion control limits. Non-CPU lens data required.

sources.name: Nikon Z-mount (Wikipedia mirror, wiki.riteme.site)
sources.findings: Metering, IBIS and EXIF work with any F lens. AF only with AF-I, AF-S and AF-P. Z TCs cannot be used with the FTZ. The FTZ II drops the tripod foot.

sources.name: J.M. Peltier: Manual focus subject detection on Nikon Z
sources.findings: MF subject detection works with CPU and non-CPU F lenses. ERF works with CPU lenses that pass distance data. AF-D lenses are uncertain.

research_notes: The 3-axis (yaw, pitch, roll) IBIS claim for non-VR F lenses comes from Nikon's FTZ II product page as cited in the existing lens record f-af-micro-60-f28d. That page could not be re-fetched in this run (Nikon product pages returned errors), so no URL is listed. The 'A and M only' entries for 'Other AF' and AI-P lenses come from a partly garbled PDF table; the PDF text explicitly confirms them for non-CPU and PC Micro lenses. The FTZ II's own weight and dimensions were not captured. Third-party F lenses are not covered by Nikon. The mounts of the Zeiss, Voigtländer and Tokina lenses should be confirmed against the kit. The web search budget ran out before third-party lens behavior on the FTZ II could be researched.
